page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-64 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 256 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage options.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, scoring in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core tests. Cryptographic and mathematical operations are highly efficient, supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets such as AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, alongside AVX and FMA. Memory performance is mixed; while small-block cached read bandwidth is exceptionally high, large-block uncached read and write operations fall into the average tier. Database operations and Redis SET performance are highly competitive, registering in the top 25% of tested configurations.

The server exhibits a clear performance tradeoff when handling large-scale machine learning tasks. While text generation with small language models is highly efficient, processing large 70B models results in poor text generation speeds, making it less suitable for heavy LLM inference without GPU acceleration. Given its balanced resource density and strong multi-core execution, this instance is well-suited for enterprise web serving, multi-threaded software compilation, relational database hosting, and general-purpose containerized workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-64 is a general-purpose server configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs and 256 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor on the x86_64 architecture. Featuring 32 physical cores with multithreading, it delivers a balanced 4 GB of memory per vCPU. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. In benchmark testing, it exhibits strong multi-core CPU performance, high-speed cryptographic execution, and excellent database operation throughput, placing it in the top tier for multi-threaded workloads. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks and text generation for large language models are limited. Supported by 32 MB of L3 cache and hardware-accelerated instruction sets like AES and AVX, this server is highly effective for multi-threaded software compilation, database hosting, and enterprise-scale general-purpose workloads.
